anchors.name: i3322_npa_level_1
anchors.derivation: Flora et al., Moment optimization in the Navascues-Pironio-Acin hierarchy, section 3.1: 'the NPA1 relaxation gives 0.375 000 01'. Independently reproduced here: the level-1 dual of the same functional, after converting it out of the Collins-Gisin picture, gives 0.37500000.

anchors.name: i3322_npa_level_2
anchors.derivation: Same paper, same section: 'and NPA2 gives 0.251 021 73'. Used as the target worth 1 on the scale, not as a ceiling.

anchors.name: i3322_best_known_quantum_value
anchors.derivation: Same paper, same section: 'the best currently known quantum value is approximately 0.250 875 38, obtained at NPA4 or higher'. This is the value the score measures distance to. It is a supremum: arXiv:2608.29734 shows it is not attained in any finite dimension.

anchors.name: i3322_classical_bound
anchors.derivation: Same paper, same section: 'The classical bound is 0'. Used here as a transcription check rather than as a score anchor - exhaustive enumeration over the 64 deterministic strategies of the converted correlator form returns exactly 0, which is what confirms eq. (18) is Collins-Gisin probabilities and not the +-1 correlators the paper's wording suggests.

anchors.name: i3322_qubit_bound
anchors.derivation: Pal and Vertesi, Maximal violation of the I3322 inequality using infinite dimensional quantum systems: two-qubit strategies cap at 1/4 and higher dimensions are required to exceed it. Reproduced here by numerical maximisation over two-qubit states and projective measurements, which returns 0.250000000 to nine digits. Used as a soundness check: every certificate this task scores must exceed it.

anchors.name: chsh_tsirelson_bound
anchors.derivation: Tsirelson, Quantum generalizations of Bell's inequality (1980): the CHSH quantum maximum is 2*sqrt(2). Textbook and exact. Irrational, so no rational certificate attains it, which is what makes the CHSH instance a graded rung rather than a pass/fail one.
